- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to adjust — cap forecast peak at 1.5x recent high or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model often underestimates continuation — add 2–3% buffer to forecast if sentiment > 0.3 and recent 5-day avg > 72.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from -0.5 to +0.5 in 3 days), model misreads momentum — use 7-day weighted average to dampen volatility-driven forecasts.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates near-term (first 7 days) — apply 10–15% downward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- If sentiment is consistently low (avg < -0.2) over 10+ days, model tends to ignore mean reversion — force a 2–3 day lagged mean reversion correction (e.g., forecast = 0.8 * prior + 0.2 * 30d avg).
